marks.note: R1′: the mark is the REFUND, which is `unlockOrder` — not possession of the upgrade that grants it (`onPurchase() { player[this.layer].unlockOrder = 0 }`, layers.js:1123 / 1418; s keeps 0 because s was chosen first). Measured to agree with the retired predicate at every fixture — false at M11, true at M12 and M15 — and to stay true at M16, where the retired one flips back to false.

predicateHistory.why: NOT MONOTONE. The refund upgrades are row-2 upgrades, and `t.doReset` / `e.doReset` keep `upgrades` only with q milestone 2 or a64 (layers.js:1031, 1341) — so the first `q` reset (row 3) wipes them and `hasUpgrade('t',23) && hasUpgrade('e',22)` reads FALSE again, while the refund ITSELF (unlockOrder 0, set by each upgrade's onPurchase) is permanent. Measured: the mark was reached at 14909 and had gone false again by M16 at 24236 (reset:q fired twice by then), on the same run.

marks.name: Space pool used right
marks.wall: pool = `floor(best^1.1·3+…)`; respec once if the pool is misallocated

source.reached: R1′ 2026-09-17: HOLDS AT THE FRONTIER (14131). Measured there: GP 4.26e90; next level of building 11 5.99e88 (affordable), 12 2.15e102, 13 1.47e115, 14 9.30e99 (none affordable); pool 27, all spent, buildings 14/6/3/4. The game's own target() with the pool freed gives 11→15, 12→6, 13→3, 14→4 — so ascending `buy` and the game's descending `buyMax` CONVERGE here: each building's GP target is independent of the pool and only the lowest one is pool-bound. The wall behind M13 is Generator Power, not the allocation order (which is why S1 §10a.4's highest-first row produced the same 14/6/3/4).

marks.note: R1′ sharpened: the two pool-raising upgrades, PLUS the pool fully allocated, PLUS the allocation LAW — no lower building holds a level while a higher one's next level is affordable in Generator Power. The law is the game's own autobuyer (`s.update()`: `for (i=5+i.b11; i>=1; i--) buyables[10+i].buyMax()`, layers.js:1713) and digest L2.13 ('ALWAYS prioritize the later buildings'). ⚠ NOT `target()`: layers.js:2104's `.max(1)` makes `target()` return 1 for a building whose level 0 is unaffordable (measured at the frontier: building 15 target 1, cost 1e230, GP 4.26e90), so a target()-based predicate names a level the game would never buy.

predicateHistory.why: H1 10b.2 item 2: `hasUpgrade('s',13) && hasUpgrade('s',15)` already held before M09 (s upg 11–15 since 3550), so the mark tested nothing about the POOL — the frontier run 'reached' it on its first tick (14132).

source.reached: V4 2026-09-20 (gate V4-m21 chose the pause, gate V4-fix wrote the fixture; twice equal, from `snapshots/ptr/all/M15.json` at diff 1 under the shipped table): **28058** game-s, hashGame `2cb09b3ddfdecd64`. ⚠ R2 RECORDED THIS MARK AS A WALL AND AS A BRANCH OPPOSED TO M22, AND BOTH HALVES ARE NOW CORRECTED. It is reachable with M22 on the SAME run, and what reaches it is not the `until`/`priority` R2 predicted but a non-latching PAUSE — the table key `gates`, which the loader has had since S1 and which no table on the roster had ever carried: `'reset:q': "!hasMilestone('q',4) || player.h.unlocked"`. `h` needs 1e30 Time Energy and a `q` reset wipes row 2, so the pause simply stops spending row 2 during the one stretch `q` has nothing left to unlock. Holds at the M22 fixture too, so it is monotone from its own fixture onward (every mark of the rung was re-evaluated at every later fixture — gate V4-fix).

source.reached: R3a 2026-09-20 (gate R3a-4, twice equal, from `snapshots/ptr/all/M22.json` at diff 1 under the shipped table): **30683** game-s, hashGame `b1d55495d90fb8c6` — 65 game-seconds after `challenges:h` is let in by its gate. ⚠ H11 "Upgrade Desert" FORBIDS NOTHING: its whole difficulty is three cost functions (`layers.js:2678-2692`) that multiply prestige-upgrade costs by `10^(n^2)` and their exponent by `4n^2+1`, and booster costs by `3n+1`, where n is how many are already owned. The guides' positional buy list (digest L3.10 + C10) is a human optimisation, not a rule the engine enforces — so `cheapest-first` completing it is not luck, and “a purchase the challenge forbids that the loader keeps attempting” cannot exist here. Holds at the M24 fixture.
